questions.q: Which organ is shown in this slide?
questions.explain: Wide, irregular glandular lumens with folded walls and fibromuscular stroma indicate the prostate.
questions.alt: Low-power view of many large irregular gland spaces separated by thin pink septa.

questions.q: How do the gland lumens of the prostate look?
options: Wide and irregular with folded walls
Small and round, filled with colloid
Narrow and straight, lined by goblet cells
Tightly coiled with a brush border
questions.explain: Prostatic glands have irregular, often infolded lumens.
questions.alt: Low-power view of many large irregular gland spaces separated by thin pink septa.

questions.q: Which feature, not visible here, would confirm prostate?
options: Corpora amylacea in the gland lumens
questions.explain: Corpora amylacea are round concentric secretions typical of the prostate.
questions.alt: Low-power view of many large irregular gland spaces separated by thin pink septa.

questions.q: A testicular section shows numerous tightly packed tubules lined by a stratified germinal epithelium containing cells at different stages of spermatogenesis. Which structure is being examined?
questions.explain: Seminiferous tubules are the sites of spermatogenesis and contain Sertoli cells and developing germ cells at successive stages.

questions.q: In a seminiferous tubule, which cell forms the blood–testis barrier through tight junctions and supports developing germ cells?
questions.explain: Adjacent Sertoli cells form tight junctions that divide the seminiferous epithelium into basal and adluminal compartments and help protect developing germ cells.

questions.q: A histological section shows clusters of endocrine cells in the connective tissue between seminiferous tubules. Which hormone do these cells chiefly secrete?
questions.explain: Interstitial Leydig cells, located between seminiferous tubules, produce testosterone in response to LH stimulation.

questions.q: Which feature helps distinguish the epididymal duct from seminiferous tubules on histology?
options: Pseudostratified columnar epithelium with stereocilia and a lumen containing sperm
A multilayered germinal epithelium with spermatocytes
A simple squamous lining with no muscular wall
questions.explain: The epididymal duct is lined by pseudostratified columnar epithelium with stereocilia; its lumen commonly contains sperm undergoing maturation.

questions.q: A section of the ductus deferens shows a narrow, often stellate lumen and a very thick muscular wall. What is the main function of this muscular arrangement?
options: Propulsion of sperm during ejaculation by peristaltic contraction
questions.explain: The ductus deferens has a prominent three-layered smooth-muscle coat that generates strong peristaltic contractions to propel sperm during ejaculation.
